text:
Dinesh: quick follow-up to the batcher RFC. i hacked a tiny enqueue->coordinator->batcher handshake to avoid races during batcher teardown. rough sketch and questions below.

Chloe: can you list the invariants you expect this to guarantee? e.g. no silent drops when capacity exists, and predictable drain behavior.

Dinesh: invariants i'm targeting:
- enqueue only allowed when coordinator shows headroom token for tenant
- batcher can revoke/expire tokens during graceful shutdown and must return any unconsumed credit
- overflow path must be non-blocking (best-effort) so callers can decide retry vs fail
- per-tenant burst credits to enforce fairness and limit noisy neighbors

Ben: where does token state live? coordinator vs batcher? what about restart scenarios?

Dinesh: token ownership lives in the coordinator (single source of truth). batchers acquire a token lease on startup and renew periodically. the lease carries a sequence/version so a stale batcher cannot use an old token.

Alice: sounds like an etcd lease with short TTL matches our existing patterns. TTL auto-expiry is nice if batcher crashes.

Dinesh: agreed. sample handshake (pseudo):
```
# batcher -> coordinator
POST /token/acquire {capacity: 32, tenant: "acme", instance: "i-123"}
=> {token_id: "t-42", lease_until: 1769857800, seq: 7, type: "soft"}

# enqueue path (fast path check)
POST /enqueue {tenant: "acme", payload: ...}
if coordinator.check_token(tenant) -> accept_into_fast_queue
else -> route_to_overflow()
```

Ben: i'd add an explicit token_version+revocation counter so coordinator can instantly invalidate tokens (no waiting on TTL).

Eric: what happens if a token is revoked mid-microbatch? do we let the in-flight microbatch finish or abort?

Dinesh: finish the in-flight microbatch but mark the batcher as draining: stop accepting new enqueues, return unused credit to coordinator at microbatch boundary. that keeps tail latency bounded.

Amanda: for fairness we should emit per-tenant headroom metrics and alert if a tenant consumes >X% cluster headroom for >Y minutes. otherwise leaky tenants silently starve others.

Chloe: also tolerate small soft overcommit for tail spikes. we can expose soft_headroom vs hard_headroom. soft permits best-effort fast-path enqueues but includes deprioritization hint.

Dinesh: proposal: token.types = ["soft", "hard"]. soft tokens allow enqueue into fast path but carry a penalty tag; batcher scheduler deprioritizes penalty work when congested.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: batching-handshake-v1 -> staging @ 2026-06-12T15:30:00Z :rocket:

Alice: audit requirements: token events (acquire, renew, revoke, return_unused) should be recorded with trace-id so postmortems and billing reconciliation are possible.

Dinesh: will add audit events + metrics: token_revocations/sec, headroom_utilization_p50/p95. tie everything to trace-id for cross-service correlation.

Ben: overflow queue should be bounded with per-tenant eviction (LRU) and provide quick failure path with 429 + `X-Queue-Hint: overflow-full` header so caller libraries can backoff intelligently.

Dinesh: agreed. final nits: keep coordinator lease protocol simple: acquire, renew, revoke, return_unused. i'll append etcd schema and sample curl flows to the RFC appendix. will push a draft update today. :thumbsup:
